newsitem.title: UK: Sterling settles lower in quiet Europe.
newsitem.headline: Sterling settles lower in quiet Europe.

text.p: Sterling settled lower after Tuesday's rally with traders happy to take profits and sit back to await further developments.

A weaker than expected set of industrial output data put paid to thoughts of another quick rise in interest rates with the market now thinking more along the lines of tighter fiscal, rather than tighter monetary policy.
"The surprise drop in output at the end of the last quarter should help dampen speculation about another quick hike in rates," said Jeremy Hawkins, senior economic adviser at BankAmerica.
Both industrial and manufacturing output fell 0.1 percent in March compared with market forecasts for a 0.3 percent rise in both indexes.
Revisions also pointed to a weaker industrial picture with the 0.6 percent fall in industrial output originally reported for February revised to a 0.7 percent decline.
Analysts first reaction was that the strength of sterling had begun to have an impact on exporters.
The pound was at 2.8105/15 marks and $1.6306/16 compared with and earlier 2.8190/95 and $1.6352/62 which was barely changed from 2.8180/90 and $1.6367/77 late yesterday.
The Confederation of British Industry publishes its survey of distriutive trades on Thursday and this will give a clue to the pace of spending in the high street.
Any domestic demand data that points to a build up of inflationary pressure will get the market again thinking about higher rates, analysts said.
Sterling's trade weighted index was 0.4 point lower at 100.2.
